literal: Not looking at another's wife is great strength of character; to the noble, is it only virtue? It is also exemplary conduct.
translation: Not looking with desire at another's wife is a great strength of character; for the noble, it is not only a virtue but also exemplary conduct.
modern: பிறனுடைய மனைவியை விரும்பாத பேராண்மையானது, சான்றோர்களுக்கு அறம் மட்டும் அன்று; அதுவே நிறைந்த ஒழுக்கமும் ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme quality of not desiring another man's wife. It states that such restraint is not just a basic moral virtue (அறன்) for the noble, but it represents the highest form of strength of character (பேராண்மை) and exemplary conduct (ஒழுக்கு). The word 'பேராண்மை' (great manliness) is used here not as physical strength, but as the mental fortitude to control one's desires. For those of high character, this self-control is the very definition of noble conduct.
